action: Limit which provider systems can change payment records or approve transactions, reconcile payment instructions against independent records, and report incidents to CERT-In within six hours.
exec: CERT-In says payment fraud now works through altered business records and approvals, and affects service providers and payout platforms, not only banks.
plain: India's cyber agency warns that attackers change payment records or approvals so fraudulent transfers look legitimate, and that AI-driven attack tools are being used against organisations.

sources.name: Telangana Today (IANS): CERT-In warns of AI-driven cyberattacks targeting business payment systems

summary: CERT-In advisory CIAD-2026-0062, issued 20 November 2026 and rated critical, says attackers alter business records or approval relationships and push transactions through legitimate payment workflows, not only payment APIs. It names technology service providers for government-linked payments and vendor or partner payout platforms among those affected. CERT-In says its threat hunting found AI-driven agentic offensive frameworks used against enterprises, providers, government bodies and research institutions.
title: CERT-In advisory CIAD-2026-0062: attackers abuse business payment workflows and AI-driven agentic offensive frameworks

validation.note: The CERT-In advisory page was read in full; Telangana Today (IANS) reports the same advisory.

review.note: Compared title, 20 Nov date, Critical rating, records/approval alteration, TSP and payout-platform scope, AOF statement, six-hour rule against CERT-In CIAD-2026-0062 and Telangana Today/IANS; all match

key_findings: Attackers alter business records or approval relationships, then push transactions through legitimate payment processes; payment APIs are not the only target.
Affected parties now include technology service providers for government-linked payment processes and platforms handling vendor or partner payouts, as well as banks and financial institutions.
Transactions can pass normal application and approval checks even though the underlying records were changed without authorisation.
CERT-In's threat hunting found AI-driven agentic offensive frameworks used against enterprises, service providers, government bodies and academic and research institutions.
These frameworks automate reconnaissance, credential attacks and parallel intrusion tasks by multiple agents, and adapt attack steps when blocked.
recommendations: Limit which provider systems can change payment records or approve transactions, and reconcile payment instructions against independent records.
Require independent verification for high-risk payment changes and agree log access and suspension procedures with providers.
Technology and payout providers should separate client environments, restrict admin and control-plane privileges, and monitor record changes alongside privileged activity and approvals.

Review internet-facing applications, identities, privileged and service accounts and external connections, and check logs for reconnaissance, credential use, admin activity and outbound data transfers.
Report incidents to CERT-In within six hours and unauthorised financial transactions at cybercrime.gov.in or helpline 1930.
